title: A Crown of Glory: Strengthen Thyself

sense.text:
“Keep thy heart with all diligence”: the heart is your mind. Your thoughts come into words, words become actions, over time those actions become habits, and then that starts to identify you as an individual: that’s your character. Once something is your character it is very hard to change. “For out of it are the issues of life”: your destiny is formed by these things. We know our ultimate destiny is that we all want to obtain salvation, the kingdom of heaven, and all those promises that pertain only to our people, the Israelites. But the scripture teaches that the majority of us, two-thirds, aren’t going to receive that destiny; two-thirds of us, our destiny is to burn with everybody else. And with the way things work in our head, it’s so easy for that to get lost on us.

They call it personality plasticity: most people wind up set in their ways. Many of us are influenced by our experiences, by trauma, by internal changes, and by maturation, and they’re saying that after the age of 30 you’re not able to change that much. We know nothing’s impossible with God and the power of the scriptures can move that, but it becomes more challenging; that’s like when Christ says you can’t pour new wine into old bottles. There are people later in life who have drastically turned their life around: many of our forefathers got called late in age; Abraham got called late, Moses got called late. And the other side of personality plasticity: look at everybody in the wilderness who didn’t make it, all the grown-ups, except Joshua and Caleb and their families. Their children went in, because there was hope for them. Until you die in this, or Christ returns while you’re living, you don’t know what your destiny is yet; you know what you hope for.

So don’t glaze over these verses. Meditate in the scriptures; stop and reflect on all those words. With that resistance to change, we need to be more mindful and strengthen ourselves, especially the later in life you repented into this, because you wind up with a stronger pull back: you’ve spent more time in the evil than you ever did in the good.

Diligence is careful and persistent work or effort, the quality of working carefully and with a lot of effort. You must be careful and persistent when it comes to keeping your heart, because the temptations are going to come; we’re going to be influenced by external circumstances and by what we say to ourselves. The scripture tells us to keep it in a very formulative way.

“Put away from thee a froward mouth”: this is one of the ways you keep your heart with all diligence. Froward is contrary thoughts to the scriptures. Your thoughts become your words, and once you start putting it into words, action follows behind it. The battle’s here, in the head. We’re not going to not have those things, because the spirit and the flesh are contrary, but keep it here; don’t verbalize it. Speak it into existence: that’s exactly what happens. “And perverse lips put far from thee”: keep that thing in your head and squash it in your head.

“Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee”: have a singular focus. We have a purpose, especially as men. Brothers, our purpose is to serve the Lord, to strive to save souls, to build the organized nation. In the past two classes on marriage we looked at 1 Corinthians 7: even if you’re married, be as if you’re not, and attend to the Lord. Our purpose here, brothers, is not to find play. Look at the multiple wives doctrine: what do you really think is going to happen if you go and get yourself three, four, five, six, seven wives? Where is your time for the Lord going to be? You got to render to all of them, and if you’re over 30, where is your mind going to be instead of attending to the Lord? We’re not here to seek our own pleasure or our own; we’re here to seek the will of the Father, and we got to move in that way. Keep the law as the apple of our eye.

“Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established”: ponder; it’s in the mind. You take action with your feet, but it’s in the mind.

We build up a fatigue in this walk, and once you get fatigued, that’s when you don’t keep things with diligence anymore, sometimes to the point where this becomes a revolving door for people. They go, they come, they go, they come; they had rank, they give it up, they leave, they want to come back. At some point we got to put a stop to that and show some consistency; you’re just walking in and out, bringing spirits with you.

“Turn not to the right hand nor to the left”: stay on the path. Make straight ways for your feet. “Remove thy foot from evil”: he’s been talking about up here, the mind, the whole time, so he says don’t even take that step into it.

When do we find out about the fornication, or that they fell back into alcohol, drugs or whatever? After. They never talk about it before. ‘I’ve been battling.’ Are you really battling? A lot of people, when they say they’re battling, mean they’ve been entertaining it; they’re literally dealing with it, not dealing with it like we just read. You always find out after, when it’s become words, when it’s become actions; they never come to you before. We can’t condemn nobody; that’s up to the Lord, he will have mercy on whom he will have mercy. But how much more could the preventative have been beneficial to you before you moved forward into that way.

A lot of you crazy brothers and sisters be talking to yourselves. Damn, that hit home for some. Not regular talking to yourself; it’s like Smeagol and Gollum in The Lord of the Rings, full-on discussions, even getting mad with the other person in your head. Some of y’all do it while you’re sitting right here. So we have to keep it with all diligence, and to keep your eye focused and to move, you got to know yourself. The scripture tells us we got to examine.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees”. A lot of times we look at that and say fear, but when you really examine it, it goes into battle fatigue, the endurance in this walk. Feeble, because you’re running for a while. When you’re running you’re supposed to move the arms, rotate, lift the knees, and when you start getting tired it’s harder to take your steps, harder to move that way.

“And make straight paths for your feet”: ponder the path of thy feet, like we just read in Proverbs 4. Eye on the prize; keep pressing toward the mark. “Lest that which is lame be turned out of the way”: you’re going to be in the way of anybody else that’s coming after you. They might try to help you, but you’re going to get to a point where they’re saying, listen, you’re just blocking the road now, brother. Anybody who has run, or cycled, knows it: in a narrow path you let them know you’re coming through, on your right, on your left. You’re blocking the way; I got somewhere to go, I got my eye on the prize.

sense.text:
“Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize?” Again it’s talking about that straight path, the hands that hang down and the feeble knees. You have to realize this is a race; they compare it to a race. The beautiful thing about this walk is that many people can receive a prize: not infinite, one-third. Whatever that final number is, we don’t know, but it’s one-third.

“So run, that ye may obtain”: run with a purpose. Some of you like to be bystanders, spectators in this, and the scripture teaches us that we got to be involved, that we can’t be idle, that we got to move forward. You don’t move with the urgency like there’s something to obtain in this; we’re cavalier, and this is why we keep hearing these things and this stuff keeps coming up, and it will till Christ returns. But we’re supposed to be rehearsing all those righteous things now. What we do as individuals is multiplied in the body: if a handful of us starts to get it right, then the next handful gets it right, and you’ll start to see the effects of that all over the place. That’s why it’s so critical we stay beholden to what the scriptures say about what goes on in the body, because if not, everybody will be infected, like when the zombie virus is spreading, and then everybody’s caught up in something.

“And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things”. Temperate is showing moderation or self-restraint. You set the paths, you don’t turn to the right or the left, you keep your mind with all diligence, you move temperately. When you move away from these principles, destruction comes, like the example lately with that fornication spirit. And it’s not just fornication; it’s anything you’re dealing with. You can have all this knowledge, you can even move to the realm of wisdom, and when you let purpose slip, that’s when you fall. Set your focus, keep your mind right, keep your mouth sealed, set your eye and move.

“Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.” We do it for a crown, and a crown has much significance. The crown is worn where? On your head. There’s a reason he mentions the crown, and it’s not always automatic, oh, the kingdom.
“I therefore so run, not as uncertainly”: he was not uncertain. He kept his heart, he knew himself, and he knew what he needed to stay focused on. “So fight I, not as one that beateth the air”.

“But I keep under my body”: he fights to keep under his body. That’s why the battle’s here, in the head. He keeps it under because he doesn’t want it to manifest itself in action. He talks about that in detail in Romans 7, and it sounds confusing because he’s going back and forth, but it’s that discussion going on inside, and he makes sure he keeps that thing under control. “And bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

precepts.why:
Here’s the example of letting purpose slip. “Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him”: the Lord gave him peace during his time so that he could prosper; the scripture says he’ll make even your enemies be at peace with you. Was Solomon not full of wisdom, the wisest man that ever walked the earth? “How wise wast thou in thy youth and, as a flood, filled with understanding!” “The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations”: even they went to Solomon for wisdom.

“Thou didst gather gold as tin and didst multiply silver as lead.” Gold is hard to mine, and it said when it came to him it was like finding tin. The equivalent today would be soda cans all over the place, on the street corner, in the garbage can: walk out your door and there’s a gold nugget. Silver as lead, because those are more abundant.

“Thou didst bow thy loins unto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subjection.” With all that wisdom and with all that blessing, this is an extreme, magnificent example in Solomon. If that happened to him, where do we wind up and where do we fall in that equation if we don’t keep our heart with all diligence? “Thou didst stain thy honour”: all of that doesn’t matter, because he stained his honour. “And pollute thy seed”: all these women polluted the holy seed, having offspring with heathen; he had the concubines and all of that. “So that thou broughtest wrath upon thy children, and wast grieved for thy folly. So the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom”: the split came as a result of the way Solomon moved.

He wasn’t temperate when it came to women. Everything else was on point, but he bowed his loins to women and by that he fell, because his purpose changed, even with all that wisdom. A lot of you brothers think you’re too smart for your own good, and you think your intelligence lets you rationalize things and justify yourself, rather than keeping your eye singular and focused so that you move with that purpose.

“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself”: that goes with Paul saying, lest when I have preached to others I myself should be a castaway. “There is one that sheweth wisdom in words, and is hated: he shall be destitute of all food. For grace is not given, him from the Lord, because he is deprived of all wisdom.” You’re deprived of wisdom because wisdom doesn’t allow you to move into those spaces, to entertain those ways.

And it doesn’t only happen with the big things. Solomon was the example with the women and the fornication, but some of y’all do it off of feelings, all in your emotions. A lot of you think effeminate is a man that’s a little sweet, but the way y’all be so easily provoked, so agitated and in your heads: that’s an effeminate spirit.

sense.text: This is one of my favorites; I always meditate on it. “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” Prove yourself and know yourself, but know yourself in what? “How that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates”. He dwells in us except we be reprobates, void of judgment. If we’re not applying the things he’s saying in order to keep him in us, then eventually he’ll leave, like with Solomon. It seems obvious, but it’s the ‘in you’ part that y’all are not really hitting home.

This is important to understanding the crown later. “As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten”. A lot of times chasten can mean inflict suffering, but here it’s not just punishment; he’s talking about the restraint, the subduing. Yes, there are judgments that happen, but to chasten something is to restrain it, to subdue it. You’ve heard of the chastity belt: garments they used to put on their daughters so they wouldn’t get it on while the parents were asleep; she was locked in. When Christ is in you, you have the strength to be capable to do those things. Chasten goes with temperate: moderation, restraint, to subdue, to restrain. They mean the same thing; we read temperate, we read chasten.

“Behold, I stand at the door, and knock”. If you’re an Israelite, born of the 12 tribes, this only applies for us. That’s the first thing you got to look at: it’s not for the whole world. Christ is not in anybody that just says ‘I believe in Christ’; he came but for the lost sheep of the house of Israel. ‘My sheep hear my voice’: he’s here only for Israel, so he ain’t knocking on everybody’s door.

“If any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.” That goes into Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates. When is the knock? When you repented, when you received this word: that was the spirit of Christ coming to you. If it was a video that grabbed you, if it was a brother or sister that gave you a flyer, Christ was knocking and he chose that messenger. So we all have that time and chance.

He knocks and he comes in, and he’ll sup with you: to sup with you means he’s hanging out, you’re serving him dinner. But here’s the thing: you have to keep him there.

Christ knocks for every Israelite, and he chooses his messenger: if it was a video that grabbed you, if it was a brother or sister that gave you a flyer, that was Christ knocking. So we all have that time and chance.

“The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong”: Solomon called it a race, and Paul called it a race. “But time and chance happeneth to them all”: time and chance for that knock to come for all Israelites, and to see if Christ is going to come in you.

But here’s the thing: you have to keep him there. He says he’ll knock and come in and sup with you. To sup with you means he’s hanging out, you’re serving him dinner. You have to keep him there.

“The righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God”: as we walk this earth, everything is in the hand of God, good or evil, righteous or unrighteous, even if you think you’re wise.

“No man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them”: none of us really understand love or hatred except by God. We had not known love; we love because he loved us first. We know those things by what the scriptures say. Otherwise you have a perversion of what you think love is, taught from polluted sources and places, but the scripture tells us what real love is.

“All things come alike to all”: everybody in Israel has that chance. Nothing has befallen us but such as is common to man. “There is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean.”

“As is the good, so is the sinner”: the good have their portion and the sinner has his portion.

The “one event unto all” is this: are you going to repent, are you going to allow Christ to remain in you, or are you going to continue to be reprobate? All sin can be forgiven, but you’re tainted every time you deal with it, and when you deal with it over and over you weaken yourself. You don’t stay strong in this. Fighting the same demon for five years, six years, seven years: the fact that it has gone on that long tells you you’re losing. And we don’t know what that dispensation is before God gives you over to a reprobate mind.

“The heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live”: we’ve got madness in our heart. This is why you have to keep your heart with diligence, focus yourself, set your paths and move the way you need to move.

“For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope.” This goes into Romans 9, where they are not all Israel which are Israel. You can’t rest your hat on just your identity. It is better that you’re a living dog than a dead one, the dead meaning you’re reserved to destruction. But all that is joined to the living has hope.

“For the living know that they shall die”: we all have to die a mortal death. “But the dead know not any thing”: there is no knowledge in the grave, there’s nothing. Do everything now, because all of it is going to be gone.

Now is the time you’re going to be able to make your mark and make your calling and election sure: not when you’re dead, not on your deathbed. When you’re dead you’re at rest, and that’s it; there is no more opportunity to prove your own self. So we do it while we walk here. Physically the battle is here while we’re living, and spiritually and physically it’s in your head.

“Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished”: all your feelings, all your emotions, all of that is gone when you drop dead. Make the most of it while you’re here. “Neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun”: he’s talking about when you’re physically here, the physical manifestation of yourself here.

“Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.” He says live joyfully and do these things, but understand that you still have all of this to account for. You have a dispensation of time while you’re here to prove yourself worthy of what the Lord has promised us. Our purpose is to serve the Lord; anything else is just a bonus.

Some of you get so caught up on the socialization. Some of you only endure here because you like the community you have. Some of y’all have been here ten years and your scriptures suck: you don’t use scriptures, you don’t talk about scriptures. A lot of sisters are like that, eight, nine, ten year sisters who don’t know how to quote a scripture to deal with a situation, goddamn. They like the office they’re in, but there’s no building up. More time and chance will happen when you’re tried, and you’ll see if you can endure it, if you haven’t done what was needed to retain Christ in your mind.

Remember Christ knocks, comes in and sups with you, but you have to keep him there. You have to keep your heart with all diligence. So here he says “Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.”

“Let thy head lack no ointment” is not pouring oil on your head. It means let your mind always be meditating on the laws; don’t let it lack any ointment. It is having the mind of Christ, the same place we started in Proverbs 4.

“Let thy garments be always white” is your actions: moving righteously, behaving righteously. That goes back to Proverbs 4: first it started with the mind, but then it says set your feet, don’t turn to the left or the right, move forward. That’s the physical. And let thy head, your mind, be right and focused: keep it with all diligence in all things.

precepts.why:
“All they that keep it shall come to life”: all that is joined to the living has hope, and here is what joins you to life. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever.” “But such as leave it shall die.”

So you can be strong, you can be boisterous, you can say be strong in the Lord and all of that, but then you let yourself get beat down by the demons you have inside of you, to the point that the thoughts became words, the words became habits, and now that’s your character. It becomes who you are. That goes back to that plasticity, and it gets more challenging: you’re making the fight harder for yourself.

Christ is in you, prove yourself; but if you’re reprobate, he’s out. It’s like that SpongeBob meme: ‘I’mma head out.’ He gives you a dispensation of time. He knocked, he came in, you repented, and then he says, all right, I’mma head out, I ain’t staying here, there’s too much evil, there’s too much wickedness going on.

Let thy head lack no ointment: here is an example of the ointment, and why he says it. “Take thou also unto thee principal spices, of pure myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty shekels, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty shekels, and of cassia five hundred shekels.” He’s giving the recipe for this particular special anointing oil: “thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil.”

That recipe is a holy thing, and there’s a spiritual side to everything we do. But Solomon is not saying just anoint your head with an ointment like this, as if it’s as simple as making the recipe, throwing the oil on your head, and you’re holy. It was symbolic. We know what is holy: the law, it’s just and good.

So when he says keep thy head with ointment, he’s talking about your mind, the same way we started in Proverbs 4. He’s talking about having the mind of Christ. The scripture tells us we have the mind of Christ, but it won’t stay; you have to keep it there.

“And thou shalt anoint the tabernacle of the congregation therewith, and the ark of the testimony, and the table and all his vessels, and the candlestick and his vessels, and the altar of incense, and the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels.” The holy oil anointed the vessels and everything in there.

“And thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.” After the vessels, he anointed Aaron and his sons. “This shall be an holy anointing oil unto me throughout your generations.”

He uses this as an example: this is a holy anointing oil throughout your generations, and that holiness is symbolic of all that is good and just. Yes, there was a spiritual essence, if you want to say it, to an oil like that, but it is symbolic of all that is good and just. That’s why the unity of brethren is spoken of with the ointment.

When I got here to Phoenix everybody was mad because I shut the school down. Everybody would stay late after Sabbath class for dominoes and pizza and wings and drinking, playing. That was a clubhouse environment, and we had to change it and get focused on work. Later you can fellowship in those things, when we know the environment is about doing the work. The unity of brethren is supposed to be refreshing; that’s the purpose it serves, being part of a tribe and having somebody there. But remember our purpose is to serve the Lord; anything else is just a bonus.

“Let thy garments be always white”: “I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear.” The nakedness is our sin. The white raiment, letting your garment always be white, is your actions: that you keep these commandments and live. All they that keep it shall come to life; that is being joined to life.

It might sound like an oversimplification, but this is about when you get fatigued in this, because it’s obvious what we have to do. You know you’ve got to stop at a stop sign, but how many of you really do a full stop? You know you’re supposed to yield at a yield sign and let the other people go through, and here in Arizona nobody follows that thing. And you truckers know you’re not supposed to be cruising in the left lane on an uphill, no less, damn. Stay right there, bro, what’s wrong with you, slowing the whole flow up. Knowing it doesn’t mean you’re doing it. It sounds obvious, but it’s up here, in the head: that is the foundation.

“And anoint thine eyes”: he talks about garments and he talks about anointing, the same two things as Ecclesiastes 9:8.

“I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation”: the same garments as let your garments be always white, and buy of him white raiment. “He hath covered me with the robe of righteousness”: that is keeping these laws, because the laws are righteousness. The priest’s lips keep that knowledge, and we learn righteousness from them.

“As a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels”: this is talking about a wedding.

The robes of righteousness are what the white speaks of, not the cloth. A man can wear white and be evil as hell; look at all them puffy white parties. Diddy, why? Are you good?

“He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment”: overcometh what? Overcometh sin. That is the white garment.

“And I will not blot out his name out of the book of life”: them that are joined to the living have hope, as we read in Ecclesiastes 9. “But I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.”

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life”: he that endureth temptation is he that overcometh, and then we will receive that spiritual body. In the spiritual, the white raiment is really talking about that spiritual body, because this flesh is not going to inherit the kingdom of heaven. But we practice those things now; we rehearse the righteous now.

Take a wedding, because that is what Isaiah 61 was talking about. You have the full rehearsal, and people try on the outfits. You don’t just get the garment and show up at the wedding: what if something’s wrong with it? Sisters are going to make sure they try on the dress; they buy it two sizes smaller in anticipation of the day. So we have this process where we are supposed to rehearse these things and move this way in them.

Read again: “the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.” Here it’s talking about a crown again, a crown of eternal life. A crown can be the physical crown, and a crown can be the top of your head, in reference to your head. That is why all these things are spoken of together: crown and head are sometimes interchangeable.

“Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness”: so there’s a crown of life and there’s a crown of righteousness. “Which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.” The only ones that will love his appearing are the ones doing his will; for everybody else it’s not going to go down that way. Can the righteous crown be given to someone who lived unrighteously? No.

Bishop Kani said last week that a lot of people talk about how we’re going to be righteous in the kingdom, but you can’t be evil and think you’re going to get there. The righteousness happens here; this is the preparation for it. This physical body is not going to inherit it, but in our mind and in our hearts we have our soul, and it is either going to be righteous or contaminated, polluted and evil. The sin you do with your body affects your soul.

Keep entertaining stuff and you start to lose the fight. It’s the same conversations over and over, the same BS all the time, to the point you’ve convinced yourself it’s everybody else: five or six different brothers and sisters you have issues with, on five or six different occasions. One person having an issue with you could very likely happen; two, possibly; three or more? Who has that much time? What is this, high school, junior high, elementary? There may be cliques, but it’s less likely. Start keeping your heart with diligence. Take a step back and say, damn, when am I going to really look at myself and say what the hell is going on, and fix whatever is there, because life and death is at stake. You don’t just get a righteous crown that day and that’s the end of it. Something has to happen first.

Let thy head lack no ointment; stay on the idea of the mind, the head. “But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you”: that anointing came with the understanding we received of Christ. We were shown the physical example of an anointing oil, and it was symbolic of the anointing we would receive from Christ, in our head and in our members.

“And ye need not that any man teach you”: that doesn’t mean ‘oh, the spirit’s going to teach me stuff.’ You don’t need any man to teach you these things because we have the mind of Christ; you know that Jesus Christ is in you except you be reprobate. “But as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him”: because it taught you, you should abide in him. Anointing with oil and no action behind it means nothing.

“And now, little children, abide in him; that, when he shall appear, we may have confidence, and not be ashamed before him at his coming.” At his appearing we’re going to rejoice, but not everybody: those that abided in him, those that were anointed. They won’t be ashamed because they had their white garments on, they didn’t lack ointment in their head, they kept their heart with all diligence and kept their minds right, and in turn that kept their habits, their character and their actions a certain way.

Christ means the anointed one: in Hebrew it is messiah, and in Greek it is anointed. As Bishop Nathanyel has gone over before, Christians does not mean a follower of Christ; it means the anointed ones. That is where they twisted it. He knocked, he came inside, but are you going to keep him there? That is the other fallacy of Christianity: they never retain any kind of righteousness or holiness.

To anoint is to confer a holy office on a priest or a monarch, and a monarch means dealing with crowns. And anoint also means sanctify: to set apart or declare as holy, to consecrate, free from sin and purified. That anointing represents retaining Christ in our minds, in our head, having him as our head.

“And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments”: this is how we know that we abide in him, and this is how you display yourself as an anointed one, as keeping ointment in your head. “He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” “But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him”: that is having that mind and keeping it with diligence.

“He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” He was tempted face to face by Satan, and did he give in? No. He kept his mind on the scriptures and used the scriptures to strengthen him to deal with it. That example is before us.

“If ye know that he is righteous, ye know that every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.” If you know he is righteous, keeping the law, then everybody that keeps the law is born of him.

Go all the way back to 2 Corinthians 13:5: prove your own selves, that Christ is in you except ye be reprobate. Now you connect the dots and understand what that really means. You can walk around and say he’s in you all you want, but when the time comes to step up and show it, you’re not doing it; you let yourself give in to your lust and your desires, whatever it is you deal with. And it all starts there, in your head.

“But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts”: to be anointed is to sanctify, because anoint also means sanctify. Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, in your mind. “And be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear.”

“Having a good conscience”: again dealing with the head, the mind. To be anointed, to be sanctified, to have that crown, so that your head doesn’t lack ointment, is having a good conscience.

“That, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.” For example, they tried to clown us for Halloween, like we’re evil for not keeping that nonsense and speaking against it, like we’re evil for wearing fringes, like we’re evil for the dietary law. Even if they don’t believe it, it’s not an evil thing we do, but they act like they’re fighting evil. They falsely accuse our good conversation.

sense.text: “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave”: you won’t be able to do it then. You have to do it now. You have to rehearse it and get yourself together now, because if you wait you’re not going to get in there. Remember 1 John 2: them that abided in him won’t be ashamed.

“Time and chance happeneth to them all”: time and chance happens to all Israelites. You’re going to get that knock, and you’re going to see if you allow Christ to sup with you, because you let him in.

Remember Mark 4, where they endure for a time. A time could be fifteen, twenty years, because if it’s not to the end you can’t say what that time is. A lot of people break it down as a few years, but it could be a lifetime, and you stumble at the end, you stumble at your end.

“For man also knoweth not his time”: we don’t know when that time is going to be. That’s why David said teach us to number our days. “As the fishes that are taken in an evil net”: a fish doesn’t know when is his last swim; he goes up to catch the bait thinking he’s just getting a meal, and next thing you know, oh my gosh, what’s going on. “And as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time.”

We are snared in an evil time. When the Greek came into power, evils were multiplied in the earth, and since then we’re in an evil time. We live in evil times, we live in hard times. Hard times create strong men. But here’s the subtlety of the evil times we’re in: there is deceitfulness in the sin that creates complacency in how we move. Even with all this in front of us, it can damage you, and you don’t know when you’re going to get caught up.

There are strong men here, and strong men create good times. Because of their labors, y’all jumped on a moving train. Y’all didn’t see the challenges and struggles as we came up. Many of you come in and have beautiful sanctuaries to be a part of, all these offices covered, systems in place, government, uniformity, but y’all weren’t there for those struggles, so it’s hard to have an appreciation for what came before. It’s like when people win the lotto and wind up broke again, versus people who built it up through sweat and tears and have more respect for it.

Good times create weak men, and it’s harder to find strong men in those circumstances. Very few of the brothers here now would have been able to handle how things were, and the leadership that was here before would say the same about back then. It’s all perspective, but there ain’t no way, boy, some of y’all would have been enduring through that stuff. And weak men create hard times: the one that’s lame and in the way, slowing the whole flow down, has to be thrown off to the side.

“When it falleth suddenly upon them”: that is the evil time.

precepts.why:
A good precept for the hard times and the strong men. “I sent you to reap that whereon ye bestowed no labour”: some of you are coming after, and you weren’t here for the foundation. That doesn’t mean there’s not a place for you, but sometimes there’s a lack of appreciation for what came before, and you don’t have that same diligence or respect for those things.

“Other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours.” In some respect it’s supposed to be that way: Christ labored, he is the chief cornerstone, then the foundation of the apostles, and then we come after that. But not everybody is trying to build the same house. That’s how strong men create good times: oh snap, this house is almost finished, I’ll come help with the roof, I’ll come throw some windows on, and meanwhile you’re doing something else that has nothing to do with what we’re trying to build, creating issues and creating problems.

Men are living in those evil times. “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest”: we’re not here to enjoy ourselves. You may have joy in this life, and that’s what Ecclesiastes 9 goes through, but that joyfulness can become a distraction if you’re not always clothed in your white raiment and your head lacks ointment. You start to focus on things and you lose: the minute you lose purpose is when you fall. You start talking about I don’t feel like this or that, you remove yourself from offices, you get sensual, you start to separate yourself and exalt yourself. It’s like a syndrome, and it goes on and on, and then comes the phone call: ‘man, I messed up.’

Then some of these brothers are put out like the scriptures command us, and they still ain’t getting it. They never show godly sorrow and never acknowledge their offense. We have a brother out like that now: with all the coaching, he still never showed any godly sorrow for the sin he committed, and then talks about it being up to us when he comes back. Talking about all types of other stuff except the sin he did and what he learned from it. I don’t want to know how you went grocery shopping this week; get out of here with that nonsense. Talk to me about where your godly sorrow is for the sins and offenses you committed, what you learned from them, and how you’re going to come back here and not spread that spirit to somebody else.

We’re in those evil times, and people aren’t moving; they’re not keeping the ointment in their head. So we have to flee from this place. “Because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction”: you’re going to get caught up in that evil net. You think that because you’re moving in holiness, at least for a time, the pollution doesn’t affect you, but there’s a limit to how much exposure you can have to this place before it starts to wear on you. If you keep the battle here, in the head, before it moves into those other things, you’re going to be better for it.

sense.text:
“Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.” Christ comes in to “sup with him”, and that means you have to keep him there. Letting him in is not the end of it; the work is keeping him in.

We are going to equip you with more than this, but it starts in the head. If you keep the battle there, before it moves into those other things, you will be better for it.

precepts.why:
“For froward thoughts separate from God”: remember the froward mouth we spoke about in the beginning, in Proverbs 4. It is all in here, in the head. The battle is here, brothers and sisters, because here is where it is conceived. Any sin you commit starts in your head first, and that means there is a chance to stop it.

It is not like Minority Report, where they arrested people for what they thought about. In that movie the precogs could see the likelihood that somebody was thinking about committing a crime, and they arrested them before they did anything, and there was controversy over it: how you going to arrest somebody before they did something? That is not having grace. We have that grace: those things are going to come into your mind. But you have to strengthen that mind. You have to move with a crown; you have to have Christ in you.

“For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.” Wisdom is Christ. He will come in and sup with you, but he is not going to stay in a body that is subject unto sin. He will walk with you for a while by crooked ways and all that stuff, but he ain’t going to go in you until you get yourself right and maintain those things.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit”. Why does it say discipline? Because it requires not letting those thoughts move to action. We are all tempted, we are all tried, but we should have the discipline, regardless of the circumstances, not to let those things be the reason why we fall.

It will “remove from thoughts that are without understanding”: it ain’t going to stay there. You start talking crazy to yourself and there ain’t going to be no wisdom in your thoughts. Even if you can pull a scripture to try to pair with the nonsense you are saying, it starts not to make sense: bro, what you’re saying doesn’t apply, because of this, this and this. That is the too-smart-for-their-own-good brothers that try to come up to us and do that stuff. And it “will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in”: that’s when he says, I’m heading out.

“For wisdom is a loving spirit; and will not acquit a blasphemer of his words”. The wisdom should be there if you keep the ointment in your head and don’t go to the left or the right, and it is not going to let those thoughts slide. So if you are entertaining some thoughts, even if they have not become actions yet, and they are not purged out of you, there is no wisdom inside of you, because wisdom would show you that what you are thinking is crazy: brother, you need to stop it.

That is how you get to the point where you become clean and swept, and it comes back with seven spirits, takes a look and says, oh all right, damn, the door’s unlocked. When the spirit of Christ ran out he wasn’t even trying to close the door: you bugged out, I’m leaving. That leaves you bare open. That is how you return to your vomit; that is how you can be in this, speak so boldly, and wind up out there in all types of wickedness, back into evil. The vomit is your sin; the evil is the pollution we spoke about. You wonder how. It is real simple: you lost the game up here. The battle was here, you didn’t maintain it, because you were reprobate and you didn’t keep Christ in your mind.

sense.text:
A crown can be the physical crown, the ornamental headdress of a monarch, the symbol of authority. But a crown is also the top of something, the top of the head. So it deals with the head, with everything up here. When it says let thy head lack no ointment, it is dealing with the mind: having the mind of Christ, which is applying these laws even before the sin starts to form in your mind, so that those things don’t get to come in. But we don’t tend to do that, and here is an example.

“Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”. A crown don’t always have to be a good thing. You think crown and you think it is a good thing, but here it is a crown of pride. He ain’t talking about drinking; he is talking about drunken sin, drunken evil.

“Whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine”. The valleys mean all the northern kingdom. This is specifically talking about the northern kingdom, but it applies to all of us, all Israel. The whole head can be sick and the heart faint, and that is how the northern kingdom was, but that is how all Israel is in these last days.

All this was being said about Ephraim while Judah, the southern kingdom, was still maintaining. But once Babylon came up, that was it: they went into captivity too, because they started to go off. It is in Ecclesiasticus also, where it says all the kings were deficient except David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

precepts.why:
What is a crown of pride? The crown deals with the head, so what was in the head? “That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. That is the crown of pride: the evil thoughts.

And out of them come “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

So you can have a crown of pride that makes you think you got this, that makes you think you know better, that you can walk alone, not realizing that Satan is roaming about seeing who he can devour.

sense.text: Here we come back to how this crown of pride can affect you. “Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees”: don’t let yourself fall into the way you saw in the example of our forefathers, with a crown of pride. Lift up the hands and the feeble knees and keep pressing forward.

“And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.” It uses the term healed here, and the scripture talks about the healing of the nations. But when it comes to men: what is a man in the process of healing? Usually laying down, out of commission, on the sidelines. As men in this fight, we don’t have time for healing.

There is a certain measure of understanding for those who are just coming in and the sick state they are coming out of. But men got to be strong; men got to strengthen themselves. Put some spit on that and keep going; bind it up, throw some dirt on it, that’s it, and keep fighting.

Proverbs 4 is saying the same thing as Hebrews 12: set yourself and keep moving, don’t let yourself go from one side to the other, lift it up and keep running the race, and move the way you need to move.

This applies to sisters to some extent too, but here the teaching shifts to the men.

“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. As men, our job is to reprove our people. Notice it don’t say neglect your house and reprove your people; it says set your house in order and reprove thy people. So we have something to do in that regard as well.

You don’t have time to be sitting on the sidelines in your feelings. Like Bishop Kani was saying: nobody cares. Oh my wife, my wife; I lost my job, this, that and the other. Guess what, that is called life. If you have some terminal illness, that is different; you come up here sick with something, we care. But regular stuff, nobody cares. That became the joke at Tabernacles.

The Apocrypha gives that example of lamenting over the death of your child. Everybody is going to lose somebody. For a season we are going to be with you and mourn with you, but it has been three months and it is still woe is me with everybody. That is for you to deal with: set your house in order and reprove your people.

“comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”: renounce that evil, that pollution, the evil times.

“Let go from thee mortal thoughts”: let go those mortal thoughts you have, the woe is me, the this is why I did that. Guess what: you got to have discipline in those situations. They might all be true, they might all be valid, but you are expected to apply discipline the same as the rest of us.

“cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature”: put off that weak nature, that effeminate nature. It is not saying don’t address the things you need to address; it says set your house in order. But don’t let those things become all the man: I got this going on, I got that, I just can’t seem to get the job I need, I can’t drop the weight, I can’t get a spouse. Nobody cares. The first or second time maybe we cared, but now it is months, years later and you are still with the same stuff.

There ain’t no scriptures that can help you if you won’t apply them. Oh, I want counsel on it; how many times? That is why some who don’t change are passed off to others to deal with. It might not be an offence where you got to be put out, but casting pearls to you when you don’t want to apply nothing, get out of here with that nonsense.

“And set aside the thoughts that are most heavy unto thee, and haste thee to flee from these times”: these evil times, these polluted times. For yet greater evils than those already seen shall be done hereafter.

You think it can’t get any worse? Did you think they would approve same-sex marriage as a law? You knew homosexuals were always in the midst, but we were saying it years ago, and now they are trying to put pedophiles into the alphabet group: they want to add the P for pedophile to the LGBTQ, normalize it, say it is a sickness in their head and we got to be compassionate to it. They tamper that type of information down until they are ready to roll something out.

They got campaign ads popping up telling everybody to vote for a candidate because she is going to let you murder your babies. We knew that abortion thing was out there, but that it would be part of a campaign so openly? All that stuff is out there, and you can’t speak against so-called Jewish people, you can’t speak against gay people. You can, but then you reap the repercussions, professionally or on social media, and for some people that is their profession. They blocked Candace Owens from entering Australia, cancelling her visa while she was on a tour, which is her job, saying it was because of anti-Semitic statements. They affected her money.

If that ain’t evil times, and that is just a fraction of the stuff that is there. It is wild, it is insane. You think we are at the pinnacle of it; more evil is coming.

precepts.why:
“Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”: you got to put those things away from you. “and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”: every thought has to be brought into that obedience that is in Christ. Remember, he is in you except you be reprobate; he resides here, in the mind. Put that stuff aside, put off now that weak nature, and bring it all into obedience. That is where the discipline applies.

Paul said he had a thorn in his side that buffeted him, and why? Because it taught him to fight. You think you are just going to boom, turn on righteousness in the kingdom and that’s it. No: you rehearse it now.

“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Set your house in order, and then reprove your people. You revenge all disobedience when your obedience is fulfilled, and that is when you are going to be effective as a leader, as a man in this walk.

“Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.” This is why we have to apply these things this way. We are in evil times, and more evil times are going to come. Put off that weak nature and be disciplined when the time comes.

Remember, the grace period has an end. You start to lose the time where you can get it right and get it together.

sense.text:
The great souled man, the magnanimous man, knew himself accurately and did not lie to himself. Grandiosity, feeling like you can do anything, believing you’re it, can be fine if it’s done in humility and meekness. But if you lie to yourself it’s going to burn your house down, because you can’t be honest with yourself: you think you can do no wrong and everybody else is wrong. That goes all the way back to keep thy heart with all diligence.

A clarifying question repeats the question, maybe with a similar word, to try to understand. A clarifying question doesn’t pull a scripture and come with a whole other thing; that’s called a Jezebel spirit, trying to get you to move away from the topic, and yes, a man could have that.

You got to be honest with yourself. Some of you sisters think you can cook certain foods: hell no. You think you’re going to put your own twist on it and make it better, and it don’t go that way. You got to know what you can’t handle. That’s a small example, but see how it can be detrimental when it comes to sin: you think you can be in an environment or a situation and resist it, and then you allow yourself to be in those scenarios. Some of you are like that with your worldly family. Nobody’s saying cut them off, but you got to be mindful of the time you’re with them and redeem the time, cleanse yourself from the pollution that was around you, because they ain’t talking no scriptures with you, and you wonder why am I carnal. It can get you jacked up in relationships too: you think you have more value than you really do, and you wonder why you always have bad relationships. Maybe it’s you.

Break the word down: magna means great, animus means soul. Magnanimous is a lofty and courageous spirit. We have to stand boldly in Christ, knowing when that day comes, with a courageous spirit to resist the temptations and apply discipline in those situations. It is nobility, high-minded and noble, and that goes to the crown. We’re dealing with our soul: having the fullness and measure of the stature of Christ in us, having that as our mind as we move forward.

“That your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment”: in knowledge and in judgment. The great souled man is able to be honest with himself; he knows himself fully and he don’t lie to himself. Some of you walk around not taking accountability for yourself, in ignorance or willful ignorance of where your opportunities are.

“That ye may approve things that are excellent”: until you’re honest with yourself you can’t look at things honestly without lying to yourself, and you can’t approve things that are excellent. “That ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ”.

“Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ”: again, the mind of Christ. That’s what we must move with; he is in you. That’s the great soul man, brothers and sisters: absent of Christ inside of you there is no great soul man. That’s the nobility. Who’s the king? Christ.

So when we talk about how we should be, it ain’t to puff yourself up. It’s to have that pride and honesty in yourself that Jesus Christ is in me, and you’ll have different moments and interactions where that’s going to manifest itself and let you show it forth. “Unto the glory and praise of God”: not for your glory and praise, but to the glory and praise of God.
“My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste”. He gives the example of eating honey, but he’s using it in similitude, as the next verse shows.

“So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul”: that’s how you magnify thy soul. The knowledge of wisdom: eat it, consume it. It’s sweet to taste, like damn, that’s a sharp precept, that’s heavy, that’s a banger, and then you show nothing forth as a magnanimous man. Zero. The scriptures say we’re a nation of kings and priests; it’s nobility, and you move in regality.

“When thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off”. Our earnest expectation is the earnest of the spirit, having Christ in you, to obtain the promises that were promised us: the kingdom of heaven, eternal life.

He also spoke about having confidence, and we always ground these things in scripture. That influencer is a so-called Christian, so he’ll think of certain scriptures, but it’s obviously not on the level of what we have and the understanding we use.

“For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end”. He is the beginning and the end, so the beginning of our confidence is that we were anointed by him and we abide in him. That’s why it says no man got to teach you anything after you’ve gotten that, because all of it is there for you.

So some of you, what else do you want? We gave you all the scriptures; we’re showing you what needs to happen for you to apply it and fight against these things. What more can I tell you? I’ve done that with married couples: you don’t want to counsel us no more? You’re damn right I don’t, because it’s all in vain; I’m just wasting my time. I love my people, I’ll make the time for you, but when I see you’re not putting the effort forth, my time is too valuable. I respect myself enough that I’m not going to waste my time in those situations anymore. Maybe if I see something change; the spirit will have to move me to enter into that situation again.

“Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation”. Have that confidence. The provocation is when we were in the wilderness and provoked the Lord to wrath and anger against us: we saw miracles, we received commandments and judgments, and all we did was rebel against them. We’re dealing with those same type of things now, just not face to face with Moses, not in that wilderness, but here where we’re at. If this isn’t our home, then it’s a wilderness, and it’s wild out there: polluted, evil times, getting snared up in an evil net.

So don’t harden your hearts. Keep that plasticity in your mind: that you’re always learning, always changing, and always have to apply discipline. Fight not as if you beat the air, and keep under your body. Don’t get so smug in your knowledge that you lie to yourself and become arrogant, because eventually you’re going to fall away by your own hand. Nobody’s going to do nothing to you there.

Knowledge puffs up. You taste that honey, it’s sweet, like damn, that’s good; but how do you get the reward from that?

“Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge”: he’s dealing specifically with food offered to idols. We know there’s no power in that; the idols ain’t nothing. “Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.” Knowledge puffs up to the point where you start to not be honest with yourself: you lie to yourself, you become arrogant, and that’s when you start to burn the house down. Just knowing, with no application, doesn’t make you wise.

precepts.why:
Wisdom though raineth down skill, and that’s when you’re living in the mind of Christ, moving that way, abiding in him. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding”, “and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” You get knowledge, but you don’t understand it fully; if you understand the power we have in our application, it’s transformative, and it opens up more things to you.

“The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord”: it starts with that, and when you start to lose the fear you forget those things. “And the branches thereof are long life.” “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”: it drives those sins from you. “And where it is present, it turneth away wrath.”

So you angry, brothers and sisters? When you have that fear and that wisdom inside of you, anger is not an emotion you use in those situations. Anger could serve you well: you see something in the street and it motivates you. That’s a righteous anger, and this ain’t talking about that. It’s talking about carnal anger, what they call a blind rage, because it dampens your wisdom and it dampens your understanding.

So what is the skill that comes with wisdom? How do you go from knowledge to wisdom? “The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright”: you use the knowledge, and you use it correctly. “But the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness”: making excuses and justifications for your sin. That’s the difference between somebody who’s knowledgeable and puffed up and somebody who has wisdom. You use the knowledge correctly, you don’t lie to yourself, you don’t make excuses, you don’t make justifications.

Some of you are so bad with that, you think you do it, but you always leave the butt. You’ll acknowledge and then leave the butt: yeah, I didn’t do it because of this, this, this, but no excuses. The fact that you have to say no excuses means there were two conversations going on inside of you. There was still that butt in there, and it messed your whole thing up.

sense.text:
The reason many of you can’t get it together, and why we struggle with the unity and moving things forward, is that you’re a spectator. You might not think of yourself as one: well, I have this office, I do flyer missions, I do this and that. But you’re a spectator, because you’re not trying to get in it with us, not really, not the way you move. You have that luxury now. Hard times create strong men, and strong men create good times. There’s not really skin in the game for you, even though your soul’s on the line, and you want to stay by the wayside. Out of necessity we lived in tribes and relied on each other; we might have had a competitive edge off of each other, but we knew we needed each other for survival. Nowadays the world is set up with so many vices that pull you away from that.

Life has become an endless supply of masturbatory substitutes for the real. You think masturbation is the direct act, but it’s for adventure too: there’s nothing that teaches you to really be a man anymore. You’re a tough guy in the video game you play, a football player or basketball player in the video game. The world is set up with distractions that let you just be a spectator. It’s the dopamine hit; you’re overstimulated, so real life doesn’t even fulfill you anymore. And it’s not just sex, it’s in everything: they’ll bring your groceries to your house, you can stay online all day, live in virtual communities with virtual friends and virtual tribes, and never have any purpose. This is how many of you don’t have the social skills to function. We make it present and easy for you; it’s y’all that give that resistance.

Men want the traditional wife, the Proverbs 31 woman; women want the romance novel, the movie they saw, The Notebook. That doesn’t mean you neglect that: you read in 1 Corinthians 7 that if you have a wife you got to consider what pleases your wife, but your priority is always the Lord. Our purpose is to serve God, brothers, not to find fulfillment in the trappings of life, because this life is an evil time: polluted, tainted, a shadow of what’s really in store for us. You find the balance in between. I go out on dates with my wife, we go places, but that’s not my emphasis, that’s not my focus. In the traditional marriage they found their joy in their everyday life. There were no movie theaters, no restaurants; there might have been a pub or an inn in the town, maybe street food, but there wasn’t this whole culture of what you think this stuff is supposed to be, and it’s destroyed us. When it says destroy you with a sore destruction, it runs the gamut from the false religions to politics to the most egregious of sins to the most subtle ways you get entrapped in those masturbatory substitutes for real things.

This is why men cannot endure. They get so fatigued in this walk because we live in a culture of instant gratification, and we have to strengthen ourselves to build that endurance. So don’t be a spectator: you have no drive, no fight, and you think you’re going to obtain anything?

“Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.” We used to live in tribes; we knew we needed each other, and we do. All we got starts with God, it starts with the Bible, but then we’re an organized nation, as a body.

“For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow”: we looked out for each other. This is why it says those that are sensual, having not the spirit, separate themselves. As men in tribes we knew we needed to rely on each other; it was life or death. Because of your masturbatory substitutes you’re under the false impression that that’s not needed, but spiritually it is, and the spiritual goes hand in hand with the physical. We move spiritually and think spiritually, but we have to enact it physically, in this place, in an evil time. “But woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.”

“If two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” So we bind together. Stop being a spectator, stop being separate, stop doing your own thing.

Some of y’all keep the Sabbath out of spite: not that anybody’s really looking at you like that, but just so we don’t think you’ve given up. Not of joy, not because you want to serve the Lord, but I’m gonna keep showing up so they can see I’m still in the fight. That which is lame is going to be moved out the way. We’re miles ahead of you, and you’re here doing the bare minimum. There’s a brother that said some nonsense like that, got no love for almost nobody here, thinking he’s going to obtain some salvation for that.

precepts.why: “Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.” It’s like we forgot that. Now you can’t even talk to a brother like a man; you can’t say something direct to him, there’s all types of offense: what do you mean by that? I mean what the hell I say, and it is what it is. I’ll tell you direct. Usually I’ll try to put some salt in my speech; sometimes I don’t, and it might come out rude, but I’ll tell you what it is, and there ain’t no ulterior motive. It’s a rough process. I know you’re feeling it now, annoyed, thinking about certain brothers.

“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”: it’s about unity. We’re talking about strengthening ourselves, and we’ve gone through various aspects of it: you got to be with the body. Exhort one another daily while it’s called today, not tomorrow, not the next day. Don’t sit on issues and problems. We have to start acting like our lives depend on it, because they do.

“Lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”: the deceitfulness of sin is the masturbatory substitutes. They got all these things that make you feel like you have a complete life, that you have purpose, and they’re all distractions. I’ll watch a show, and the algorithms get me sometimes, but not too much; I don’t know how some of y’all got the time. It’s a substitute for what’s really there. The pleasure of sin is only for a season; we seek something greater.

Spectating is idleness, and this is what comes of that idleness. This is why you got to get in it, keep yourself fighting on the same page with us, and get in where you fit in. Not everybody has the same office or the same calling, but when they lived in tribes all of them had to do something to survive. If we got dropped on a deserted island we’d all have to work together in different offices: not everybody’s going to be the hunters, not everybody’s going to be the ones that cook; some are going to build shelter, some are going to be lookouts, some are going to be medical. Why we got to wait till we get dropped in the wilderness? Because you have masturbatory substitutes.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

sense.text: So get strong and build strength. “Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart”. It starts with the Lord. Wait on the Lord means get yourself in the frame of mind of applying and understanding what our purpose is, the way God wants that purpose to be. “Wait, I say, on the Lord.”

precepts.why: “Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the Lord.” Have that courage: he’ll strengthen your mind so that you can move the way you need to move, and have hope in the Lord.

sense.text:
Don’t be moved by anything. The only thing that should have movement in you is wisdom, and that includes your own sins: it starts with the things you’ve conceived in your mind.

“Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.” Wisdom is what’s going to strengthen more than any physicality, more than ten mighty men in the city; wisdom is what’s going to build us up. So with all we’re getting, we have to get that understanding, we have to get that wisdom.

“For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” That goes into what we were reading in Ecclesiastes 9, that time and chance is for all, the sinner and the righteous: wisdom is going to pass through all of us, whether we retain it.

“She is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty”. A pure influence means there has to be change behind it, not just knowing it; it influences your actions. “Therefore can no defiled thing fall into her”: you got to retain it, retain that spirit with you.

“The brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” It’s the unspotted mirror because you don’t lie to yourself. It’s not going to hide a blemish, it’s not going to hide the booger, it’s not going to hide that your hair’s jacked up. That’s the unspotted mirror: she will not acquit a blasphemer of their words.

“And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls”. Wisdom is Christ: he said I knock and I’ll come in and sup with you. “She maketh them friends of God, and prophets”, because through Christ is how we will eventually be able to know God.
“For God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom.” To dwell with it means to live with it: he don’t love nobody else except them that live it.

“For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it. For after this cometh night: but vice shall not prevail against wisdom.” The masturbatory substitutes shall not prevail against wisdom. You won’t fall into those vices, because you’ll apply discipline in those moments and not sin.

Don’t be moved by people or situations. Being moved by every situation is low emotional intelligence, and that is being that city without walls. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls”: you’re a broken man, a broken brother or sister. You got no walls, and every provocation incites you. It might not always be anger, but you always got something contrary to say that’s not on board with what the scriptures say. That is not the mind of Christ.

“Broken down, and without walls” means you got no defenses around you. Everything bothers you. Some come up here offended about the most ridiculous stuff, so traumatized that you have to wonder who hurt them. Emotional regulation is the skill to master: if we can’t regulate our feelings around a situation, that event has power over us instead of us over that moment. Rule your own spirit and build your walls up.

Here is the example of Elijah: the scripture says nothing moved him, not words, nothing. “Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind”: Elias is Elijah, and Eliseus, “filled with his spirit”, is Elisha.

“Whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince”: it don’t care if you were royalty, he was not moved. “Neither could any bring him into subjection”: nobody. That means not his sins, not his lust, not his desires; he was not going to be subject to them. Now those situations control people instead of them being in control. Those things move you, they become the stuff that motivates you and moves you, and it should not be that way. That’s wrong; that’s not the mind of Christ.

“No word could overcome him”: no matter what you said. Sticks and stones may break, and nothing overcame him.

“And after his death his body prophesied”: that’s literal. First there was a memorial of him, and then the times that he’s come back, he is always unmovable and always unshakable. Think of his mission when he came back in these recent times: he had to come to bring understanding back to us after we were in darkness, during the rise of all these masturbatory substitutes, with the people laughing him to shame and trying to scorn him. If he was movable, this thing wouldn’t be where we are now. He wasn’t moved. You got to build your walls up.

precepts.why:
Christ speaks “unto the multitudes concerning John”, John the Baptist, and when we get further we know who he was speaking about: Elijah. “What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?” No. Not a man moved by every wind, and not “a man clothed in soft raiment”, for “they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.”

“A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet. For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.” “Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist”, because he was not moved. So you want an example to follow after: don’t be moved by any of that.

“For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.” This is Elias, like we just read in Ecclesiasticus.

So when it says that after his death his body prophesied, there’s a memorial of him, and every time he’s come back he was unmovable. John was Elias come again, and when he came back in recent times it was somebody unmovable, because his mission was to bring understanding back to us after we were in darkness.

sense.text: “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.” Get that understanding: understanding the knowledge is the key to obtaining that wisdom.

“Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.” Wisdom is the thing that will strengthen you. That’s the foundation; that’s where it starts. And wisdom is the mind of Christ, the spirit that’s in you.

“Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her.” Remember what we read with Solomon: when he bowed his knees and put himself in subjection to women, he stained his honor. But if you stay in wisdom, it will exalt you and bring you to honor when you embrace her.

“She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace”: wisdom is an ornament of grace, and it’s shown in your actions, how you move and your reputation. “A crown of glory shall she deliver to thee”: a crown of glory will wisdom deliver to thee.

Back to Isaiah 28 to talk about this crown of glory. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower”: that crown of pride will bring you to dishonor. That glory is a fading flower.

“The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet”, because you’re going to stain your honor. And they were: we were trodden underfoot under the Assyrians. That’s when it started.

“The glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley”: we had our portions, we had our land, we had all this beauty, but we did not want to retain it. So it “shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up.” We were going to go through a time where the enemies would eat us up: eat up our heritage, eat up everything, take our identity.

Then it shifts: “In that day shall the Lord of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people”, unto the remnant of his people. A lot of times we hear ‘that day’ and think it means when Christ returns, but there are different levels to the crown we’re going to receive. This is when we return to God: we have a crown of glory upon us now, and that crown is Christ.

In that day, now in our redemption, we retain Christ in our mind and in our spirits, so that we’re not reprobates and he’s our head, the crown that we wear. That should motivate you all the more to retain that in your mind and strengthen yourself in wisdom, so that you move that way. It’s worn as a crown of wisdom to us now, and then in that day when we are redeemed we will get that real crown, in that rulership.

Just like the woman is the glory of the man, we are the glory of Christ and Christ is the glory of God. That goes into Ephesians 5, where the husband, representing Christ, presents to himself the wife, Israel, as a glorious church without spot or blemish. But we have to retain that crown and do what he told us to do.

“And for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate.” Turning the battle to the gate means we’re going to prophesy against all these nations that are here.

precepts.why:
This shows that ‘that day’ is when we return to God. “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”: without a king, without a crown. We were desolate, we were eaten up, just like we read in the beginning of Isaiah 28.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return”: afterward, after the coming of Elijah, after that understanding came back out. Return, because now we’re not calling ourselves Puerto Rican or black or Jamaican; we’re calling ourselves by our Israelite tribes. They “seek the Lord their God”, the God of the Bible, the black Messiah Jesus Christ, “and David their king”: now we’re getting a crown again.

“And shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” You’re not just going to magically poof into the kingdom and all of a sudden be righteous. We do it now. So the Lord of hosts being a crown of glory in that day is a crown we have upon us now, and that crown is Christ.

“Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” That is turning the battle to the gate: we go into the gates of the nobles and we speak against principalities.

That lets you know that the crown of glory is now, and that crown of glory is the spirit of Christ that sits in us. That is what the Lord of hosts being for a crown of glory goes into. And that is what we were told to do with that crown: go to the gates of the nobles.

We go to this a lot just to say, look, woman, and it’s true, but there’s something else in it that we don’t think about when it pertains to us. “But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ”, and that has significance. Christ is our head, and he’s our crown of glory, because we’re led by him. Just like the woman’s desire is unto us and her mind should be on our mind, our mind and our desires are to Christ and on his mind. If he’s our head, he’s our crown, just like we’re supposed to be the head to them. Supposed to be, because though they don’t embrace it, we are.

“And the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” The head of Christ is God: it’s the same thing as where Christ says he can of his own self do nothing, but does the will of his Father.

“For a man indeed ought not to cover his head”, because we’re already crowned, “forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.”
